title: Mathai Joseph vs Marikutty Joseph on 19 December, 2012

paragraphs.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF KERALA AT ERNAKULAM

 PRESENT:

 THE HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE PIUS C.KURIAKOSE
 &
 THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE BABU MATHEW P.JOSEPH

 WEDNESDAY, THE 19TH DAY OF DECEMBER 2012/28TH AGRAHAYANA 1934

 Mat.Appeal.No. 617 of 2010 ( )
 ------------------------------
 OP NO.914/2008 of FAMILY COURT, KOTTAYAM

APPELLANT(S)/RESPONDENT:
-------------------------

 MATHAI JOSEPH, AGED 51 YEARS, S/O.MATHAI
 RESIDING AT KAKKATT HOUSE, KATTAPPANA P.O.
 PARAKKADAVU, UDAMBANCHOLA TALUK, IDUKKI DISTRICT.

 BY ADV. SRI.JOICE GEORGE

RESPONDENT(S)/PETITIONER:
------------------------

 MARIKUTTY JOSEPH, AGED ABOUT 47 YEARS,
 W/O.MATHAI JOSEPH, RESIDING AT MANIMALAKUNNEL (H)
 NARIYANI P.O.,ELAMKULAM VILLAGE, KANJIRAPPALLY
 TALUK, KOTTAYAM DISTRICT-PIN-686506

 R, BY ADV. SRI.SURIN GEORGE IPE

 THIS MATRIMONIAL APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON
19-12-2012, ALONG WITH MA. 715/2010, RPFC. 270/2010, THE COURT ON THE
SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:



 PIUS C. KURIAKOSE
 &
 BABU MATHEW P. JOSEPH, JJ.
 ----------------------------------------------------
 Mat. Appeal Nos. 617 & 715 OF 2010 and
 R.P.(FC) No.270 of 2010
 -----------------------------------------------------

 Dated this the 19th day of December, 2012

 J U D G M E N T

PIUS C. KURIAKOSE, J



 The parties to the above cases have compromised all the

issues between them. A written compromise signed by them

and attested by the respective counsel is filed. They also pray

that the matrimony between them be dissolved in terms of S.10

(A) of the Indian Divorce Act.

2. We have gone through the compromise as well as the

petition under Section 10(A) . All necessary ingredients for

granting a divorce under Section 10(A) are agreed upon by the

parties in their compromise petition. It is stated by the parties

that they are convinced that the matrimony between them has

Mat. Appeal Nos. 617 & 715 OF 2010 and
R.P.(FC) No.270 of 2010
 -:2:-

become irretrievably broken down and they have realized that

continuance of the matrimonial bond will not be useful to either

of them. There is no collusion between them in the matter of

mutual divorce agreed between them. It is averred that

unsuccessful attempts for resolution of marriage were made. It

is also averred in the compromise petition that in full and final

settlement of all the claims the wife, Smt.Mary has received an

amount of Rs.17,00,000/-(Rupees Seventeen Lakhs only) from

the husband, Sri.Joseph. Under the above circumstances, we

record the compromise and order that the matrimony between

the appellant in Mat. Appeal No.715 of 2010 and the respondent

therein is liable to be dissolved by a decree of divorce in terms

of S.10(A) . We, therefore, allow Mat. Appeal No. 617 of 2010 in

view of the compromise and the payment. The impugned order

in Mat. Appeal No.617 of 2010 is set aside.

3. R.P.(FC) 270 of 2010 is also allowed and the order in

M.C.No.256 of 2008 impugned in the R.P.(FC) is set aside.

Mat. Appeal Nos. 617 & 715 OF 2010 and
R.P.(FC) No.270 of 2010
 -:3:-

 Post Mat. Appeal No.715 of 2010 on 20th June, 2013.

Presence of the parties is not necessary on that date.

Sd/- (PIUS C. KURIAKOSE, JUDGE)

 Sd/- (BABU MATHEW P. JOSEPH, JUDGE)
ul/-
